Semantic changes of the resolved policy, and argv order, change the right digest

clauses.clause: A semantic change in a canonical TOML input (a limit, grant or environment value) changes the policy digest, and only the right one
clauses.note: Through resolve_plan over real files: a limit or grant changed in the canonical TOML profile, or an environment value in a launch profile, changes the policy digest; comments/blank lines do not; the argv digest is independent.

Raising the memory or CPU ceiling refuses with that limit key

clauses.clause: Weakening coverage, evidence or observation refuses
A project file may not select or extend a profile
clauses.note: Through ouro-jail run: policy_widening at jail.profile / jail.extends, exit 125, nothing prepared. Red when resolve_plan's forbidden-key detection is removed.

clauses.clause: Adding a credential through a project file refuses with its key path

clauses.note: launch.credentials and launch.network.allow under tool, and --launch under none. Narrowed to launch profiles (integrator decision, J5 wave 3): no v1 configuration layer has an executable or backend key (§6.3 last paragraph, §12 'path references, never commands'), so that half has nothing to refuse.

clauses.note: The child truncates the operator profile file selected with --profile (in its workspace) and the project file; digest, mounts and both denials hold.

clauses.note: Owned by J5-B1.

clauses.note: Machine-distinct: (outcome.cause, outcome.error.code) = (ENOENT, exec_failed), (ENOENT, exec_interpreter_missing), (EACCES, exec_failed). New code exec_interpreter_missing; proposed text in j5/B1/spec-proposal.md.

clauses.clause: With observation off, a target exec that cannot be confirmed is a coded tool error (exit 1, exec_unconfirmed in errors[] and one stderr line), never a bare unknown; a confirmed one exits as the target did
clauses.note: Found by the J5-C and J5-E reviews (§6.4). New code exec_unconfirmed; proposed text in j5/B1/spec-proposal.md. The integrator may prefer to file it under another gate.

clauses.clause: Large stdout/stderr and binary bytes match direct execution byte for byte
Under none, EOF on stdout reaches the caller when the target closes it, as in direct execution
clauses.note: Product fix (J5-B1): the supervisor kept its own stdout copy for the whole run. The portable test guards that releasing stdout is the binary's opt-in, not the library's (in-process use). The contained profiles, and stderr, are X05.4's recorded limit.

clauses.clause: Control and trace frames never leak into either stream
Under tool, agent and build, EOF on stdout and stderr, and under none EOF on stderr, reach the caller when the target closes them, as in direct execution
clauses.limit: docs/specs/jail-v1/j5-authority.md § Known gaps: Under the contained profiles bubblewrap's outer process and namespace init hold the stdout and stderr they hand the target until the jail exits, so the caller's end-of-file comes when the jail exits, not when the target closes its streams. The supervisor also keeps its own stderr, which carries its diagnostics.
clauses.note: Integrator decision (J5 wave 3): the contained half of the EOF claim, and stderr under none (it carries the supervisor's diagnostics). The none stdout half is X05.3.

clauses.clause: No private descriptor or reserved environment reaches the target under tool, agent or none
CapEff is empty under tool; CapPrm and CapAmb are empty under none
CapPrm, CapInh, CapBnd and CapAmb are empty for every contained profile
clauses.note: Owned by J5-B1.

clauses.clause: No tracing privilege: ptrace and pidfd_getfd against the supervisor and observer fail
clauses.note: Direct proof (r05_the_supervisors_own_proc): under none — where the supervisor is a reachable same-uid ancestor — the child cannot open the supervisor's /proc/<pid>/environ or /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> (its live trace/control channels), cannot reopen those channels, and cannot ptrace-seize it; all fail EACCES/EPERM. Under tool the supervisor is outside the child's pid namespace and not addressable. Mutation-provable via the PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 hardening in supervisor.rs run (removed -> the child reads the supervisor's environ/fd and ptraces it, verified RED on host); the lock is the kernel dumpable check, not host Yama (which a peer can waive with PR_SET_PTRACER). The contained test (x06_no_tracing) proves, from inside tool/build/agent, that pidfd_getfd/ptrace against every process the child can address (its own bwrap init, agent launcher/bridge) fail and that the /proc it sees is its pid namespace only; mutation-provable via the capability drop (child CapEff/CapPrm/CapInh/CapAmb empty; adding CAP_SYS_PTRACE with the CapEff verify disabled reddens it). It no longer probes none, which is uncontained (its child is a normal same-uid process that may address and ptrace unrelated same-uid peers — the guarantee that matters there is the supervisor's, above). Fixes the earlier version that never called pidfd_getfd, targeted a pid absent from the child's namespace, and blanket-asserted over unrelated host processes under none.

clauses.clause: Target exit with background descendants terminates them: the descendant's marker never appears, the namespace init is gone, and the receipt says so
clauses.note: Three independent mechanisms kill the tree, so the test cannot tell whether the receipt's verification is what established it (next clause).

clauses.clause: The termination is verified: a tree-emptiness claim that was not verified fails a test
clauses.note: tool, and none with observation off and on: the target exits with a background descendant while the leaf holds one more member, a process of the test's own traced with PTRACE_O_TRACEEXIT, which the supervisor's cgroup.kill reaches and which then waits at its exit stop, still a member of the leaf (measured on kernel 7.0); the run ends `unsettled`, tree_empty null, tree_unknown, exit 1, and the member was killed; released, it dies and gc removes the retained leaf. A stand-in for a member that cannot be verified dead within §9.3's budget. Red under M4 (contained wait_tree claims empty at once), M4d (it verifies the pid namespace but not the leaf) and RV1 (none takes a killed leaf for empty without reading `populated 0`: the none observation-off leg). The L01.6 test's none legs add that a real background descendant is dead before `settled` is announced (red under M4b).

clauses.clause: An allowed workspace write succeeds

A missing root-level .ouroboros is protected

Mount replacement of a protected object (unmount, rename or mount over it) fails
clauses.note: The protected object cannot be mount-replaced (mount/umount2/move_mount/open_tree/fsopen all EPERM, object unchanged, still EROFS). Two independent locks (seccomp mount deny + CapEff=0); a seccomp-only mutation is a documented green survivor.

An all_descendants requirement refuses on Linux
A new deep protected segment created at run time is outside existing_and_root coverage, and the receipt says so

clauses.clause: Scan-limit exhaustion (entries, depth, an unreadable directory) refuses rather than claiming partial coverage

Enforcement: the pin.verify() refusal loop in platform.rs; iterating no pins reddens it.

clauses.clause: Through ouro-jail run, each refusal writes a refused receipt that claims no complete boundary
clauses.note: The product's refusal paths (platform.rs) are reached by no test. Owned by J5-B2.

clauses.clause: The syscalls the baseline denies fail inside the contained child, because of the filter
clauses.note: userfaultfd, open_by_handle_at, name_to_handle_at and syslog are never exercised live (gap analysis §1.2 S01).

clauses.clause: Ordinary threads still work: clone3 answers ENOSYS and glibc falls back to clone
The child cannot see host processes (private pid namespace and /proc)
clauses.note: B2: the private /proc shows no host process, through ouro-jail run.

clauses.clause: /sys is not among the contained child's roots
No cgroup filesystem is mounted or reachable in the child
clauses.note: From inside tool/build/agent the child's /proc/self/mountinfo has no cgroup/cgroup2 mount, /sys/fs/cgroup is not a live cgroup tree, and open_tree/fsopen(cgroup2) fail. none is uncontained by definition (host view) and is not covered. Wave 5 (review F6): the MOUNT-ABSENCE assertion is mutation-provable — adding --ro-bind /sys /sys to the contained bwrap plan makes /sys/fs/cgroup (cgroup2) appear in the child's mountinfo and reddens the test (verified RED on host). Only the open_tree/fsopen(cgroup2) syscall denials are defence in depth (seccomp DENY_EPERM plus the dropped capabilities: creating a mount needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so removing the seccomp deny alone leaves them EPERM).

clauses.clause: Opening a host namespace descriptor fails
clauses.note: Covered only indirectly (private /proc; setns and unshare EPERM). Owned by J5-B2.

clauses.clause: Host sockets are unreachable: lo-only network, socket families outside the list refused, host Unix peers refused
The child cannot reach the supervisor's state

Now refused with policy_widening at filesystem.read_only/read_write, by fstatfs magic and mount topology on the resolved source (a symlink onto /proc too), before exec. The portable test covers the pure ancestor rule off Linux. Could also key under F01; S02 (host proc/sys/cgroup unreachable) is the closer §15 row.

clauses.clause: tool rejects all three io_uring interfaces and their ABI variants, so no async socket/open/connect runs
agent's baseline rejects io_uring as tool's does

clauses.note: An io_uring ring on stdout refuses before exec (exit 125, naming stdout and the anonymous inode); on stderr it also refuses before exec (the target never runs) but cannot emit its diagnostic to the ring and exits via a panic instead of 125 — a main.rs robustness gap flagged to J5-D (B2/requests.md, w4), not a containment failure. clauses.clause: agent and build inherit no ring
clauses.note: An io_uring ring created by the parent and parked at a HIGH descriptor (200) with close-on-exec cleared does not reach the agent or build target (§9.2 'No ring fd may be inherited'): the target's /proc/self/fd holds no io_uring anonymous inode. Wave 5 (review F1): the earlier version created the ring at fd 3, which the harness overwrites with its trace channel before the jail runs, so the test was vacuous; parking at fd 200 (above every channel target) makes the ring genuinely inheritable. Now single-point mutation-provable: removing close_range_cloexec() from the backend bootstrap pre-exec lets the ring reach the target (verified RED on host — bwrap does NOT close inherited descriptors, so the earlier 'bwrap fd hygiene' note was wrong).

clauses.clause: none retains its explicit io_uring exclusion: io_uring is not filtered under none
clauses.note: Named in j4-authority.md Known gaps; no live none run exercises it. Owned by J5-B2.

proc.exit means final thread-group death

clauses.clause: Under ptrace no unmatched exit occurs

clauses.clause: A process the supervisor was started beside (its own child that the attempt did not create) is not observed, is not loss and does not hold the observer open: doctor reports the observer available and an observed strict run settles verified
clauses.note: The jail is exec'd by a helper that forked a child first (the process-substitution shape, made explicit). Three tests drive the tracer in-process (live-lib): Finished beside a live child that stops and continues while traced, no gap, no unreaped child, the child still the test's to reap; an exit of such a child while traced is one UntracedChildExit and no loss; the backend the launcher descends through is still awaited and its exit delivered before Finished. Two drive the real ouro-jail (live-cli): doctor's observer_closed_set and closed_set_observation available; a strict tool run with --trace-fd to that child exits 0, settles with tree_empty true and integrity verified, every class active with no gap, and the child reads the whole stream, which passes check_trace ending in the receipt. All five were red on 91a347ad except the exit-while-traced guard.

The receipt is verified with cause wall_expiry and the wall row hit. Red under M2 (no forced stop), RV6 (the wall at release: the target is dead 2 ms after it) and RV6b (the wall at 60%: 3.2 s against the 4 s floor).

Operator TERM to a none supervisor with an intact leaf ends at verified tree death

clauses.clause: Trace partial writes resume at their offset and never tear a frame

clauses.note: The partial writes are forced by the release-binary test seam OURO_JAIL_TEST_TRACE_FD_WRITE_MAX=64 (recorded in jail state and native details). The live tests give the real jail a SOCK_SEQPACKET socket as its --trace-fd, which keeps every write(2) as one message: every message is at most 64 bytes and inside one frame, and the frames need at least that many pieces, so a binary that does not apply the seam fails (rev-late F2's M2). A slow but live consumer gets every frame (complete, passing the frozen contract, no loss) and the target ends 2 s after its exec. A stalled consumer stops reading until the socket shows the jail blocked with a frame partly written (queued bytes stable; the queued messages, peeked without consuming them, end mid-frame), holds that 1.5 s with nothing more written, past the 1 s no-progress deadline; the held frame is then finished intact from its offset or is the visibly incomplete end, and evidence_lost is recorded. Both times the wall fires on time by the receipt's own timestamps.

clauses.note: The suite runs the pinned toolchain's own cargo (not the rustup proxy, which prepends ~/.cargo/bin) under PATH=<system directories>; the listed test asserts the PATH every test process has, and the check reads the PATH line the suite's shell prints.

clauses.clause: Full jail conformance passes in that environment
No vendor name in the execution core
No protocol dependency in the execution core: its direct dependencies are the reviewed set
The bundled launch profiles are data the runtime never embeds or discovers (by literal-path scan)
Selecting a launch profile (--launch NAME) reads only the operator's configuration, with no built-in fallback
clauses.note: J5 adversarial review (rev-A) agent table: neither test drives selection.

clauses.clause: An owner that releases the attempt it was told about starts exactly one target
clauses.note: The owner's expected plan is built from the jail's own proposal (binds only attempt_id); comparing against an independent plan is I03.2.

clauses.clause: The owner compares the prepared policy digest, argv digest and requirements with its expected plan
clauses.note: The plan comes from the owner's own inputs (explain --json for digest and requirements, canonical argv framing, an attempt id it allocates), never from the receipt it judges. Red when the product writes a wrong argv_digest or drops a requirement.

clauses.clause: A mismatch closes the gate with no target marker, against the real jail
clauses.note: Tested only against the stand-in (ouro-fixture tests/harness_gate.rs). Owned by J5-B1.

clauses.clause: Untrusted request fields cannot mutate the owner's operator inputs
clauses.note: The untrusted request's argv (operator-flag look-alikes after --) leaves the owner's planned policy unchanged; its project file selecting a profile refuses before prepared; one that only narrows is caught by the owner's plan and nothing runs.

clauses.clause: A real batch agent run records revision, OS, backend, vendor version, profile and receipt, without credential archives
clauses.note: Recorded manually in agent-compatibility.md at 3c3638c4 (J3 era); re-run or explicit skip is user decision §4.4 of the J5 contract.
